learning_objectives: Explain data collection using simple language and an example.

lessons.objective: Learner can understand, explain and apply data collection.
teaching_sequence: Begin with a concrete or familiar situation.
Name the mathematical idea and connect it to prior knowledge.
Model a complete worked example with every step explained.
Move from representation to symbols and then to a new problem.
Ask the learner to explain the method without copying.
lessons.checkpoint: Explain data collection without notes and solve a new example.

items.question: Which approach best helps you understand data collection?
options: Identify what is known, represent it clearly, choose a valid method, and check the result.
Choose an operation before reading the problem.
Copy a worked answer.
Guess and stop.
items.explanation: Understanding the situation, choosing a method and checking the result makes mathematical reasoning reliable.

items.question: Explain data collection as if you were teaching it to someone learning from the basics.
items.answer: A correct response defines data collection, gives a simple example, and explains the reasoning.

items.question: Create and solve a new everyday problem involving data collection.

flashcards.back: Define data collection, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define tables, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define pictographs/bar graphs, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore data collection
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on data collection. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where tables is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach interpretation to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
